title: Benchmarking Spatial, Spectral, and Self-Supervised Cues for Face Forgery Detection under Realistic Degradation
venue: 39th Conference on Graphics, Patterns and Images (SIBGRAPI 2026)
note: Originated from my undergraduate thesis. The research continues towards a more robust version of the work.
abstract: A standardized face forgery detection benchmark on the MFFI dataset comparing six model families (CNNs, Transformers and a frozen DINOv3) across spatial, spectral (FFT) and hybrid inputs. It shows that clean-set performance is not a reliable indicator of robustness under compression, resizing and blurring: Xception with RGB leads on clean data (0.884 ROC-AUC), while frozen DINOv3 achieves the best degraded-set result (0.726 ROC-AUC) training only a linear head.

title: An Ensemble-Based Self-Taught Learning Approach for Parking Space Classification Under Limited Data
venue: IEEE International Conference on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics (SMC 2026)
abstract: A self-taught learning framework based on unsupervised representation learning with convolutional autoencoders. Encoders learned from unlabeled data are reused as fixed feature extractors, and an ensemble of heterogeneous autoencoders with prediction fusion improves robustness. Under cross-dataset evaluation on PKLot and CNRPark, it substantially reduces annotation requirements, reaching 93%–96% accuracy in data-constrained scenarios.
